title: Slow photons: light reflected from a receding surface travels at about $c - 2v$

statements.text: Light reflected from a surface moving away from the detector at local speed $v$ travels at about $c - 2v$, since the moving surface acts as the source of the outgoing light. A rotating disk is one setup, and any receding reflector would serve.
statements.conditions: A laboratory at rest in the absolute frame, a small reflection angle, and a surface speed $v < c/2$.
statements.falsification_criteria: No additional delay of the reflected pulse, beyond the path-length difference, that grows with the surface speed.

prediction.resolution_criterion: Arrival times of light reflected from a surface moving away from the detector, such as the edge of a rotating disk, are compared with a direct reference pulse, corrected for path length, with the surface stationary and at several speeds. The reflected light shows an additional delay matching a speed of about $c - 2v$.

sources.quote: the predicted reflected-light speed is approximately c − 2v for a sufficiently small reflection angle.
Compare the arrival times of reflected light and a direct reference pulse, accounting for their different path lengths.
